title: Approval with the Approver Away
scenario: It is 6:40 AM. Today's brief needs sign-off, the request went out - and the Desk Manager is out of office. The approval template names a delegate for exactly this case. Capture the response AND the substitution, because 'who was asked' and 'who answered' are different facts today.
input:
[6:39 AM] Meridian Workflow -> Desk Manager
Subject: APPROVAL NEEDED: ERCOT 15.9% - morning brief
ERCOT moved 15.9 percent day-over-day, above the 14 percent escalation threshold (policy v1.1.0). Please respond within 30 minutes.

[6:40 AM] Automatic reply from Desk Manager:
Out of office until Thursday. For desk approvals contact the Deputy Desk Manager (named delegate, approval template v1.1.0).

[6:44 AM] Meridian Workflow -> Deputy Desk Manager
Subject: APPROVAL NEEDED: ERCOT 15.9% - morning brief (delegated)

[6:47 AM] Deputy Desk Manager -> Meridian Workflow
Approved. Flag the WAUE forecast gap in the ops section.
instructions: Track the request through the redirect: who was asked first, who actually decided.
Record the substitution explicitly and its reason.
Capture the decision word and the time it arrived.
Return one JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Capture this delegated approval as JSON with hub, movePct, sentTo (the original addressee), decision, decidedBy (who actually responded), decidedAt, substitution (true), and substitutionReason. The Desk Manager was out of office; the named delegate decided.
successMessage: Delegated approval captured. The record shows who was asked, who answered, and why they differ - no archaeology required.

intro.heading: Before you build: asked and answered can differ

sections.title: Delegation is designed, not improvised
sections.body: The out-of-office reply did not send the workflow scrambling - the approval template already named a delegate. That is what governance buys: the exception path was decided before the exception happened.

sections.title: The substitution is part of the record
sections.body: An auditor seeing 'Deputy Desk Manager approved' with sentTo 'Desk Manager' and no explanation smells a control failure. substitution: true with a reason turns the same facts into a documented, legitimate delegation.

sections.title: Timeouts and redirects are normal
sections.body: Humans are the least reliable component in any workflow - not from malice, just vacations, meetings, and mornings. Mature handoffs assume this: deadline, delegate, and a record shape that can hold the detour.

fieldGuide.meaning: The move stated in the request.

fieldGuide.hint: The original addressee, not the delegate.

fieldGuide.meaning: The decision word from the reply.
fieldGuide.hint: First word of the final message.
Not the same person who was asked.

takeaway.heading: Delegated approval captured
points: You kept 'who was asked' and 'who answered' as separate facts - the difference IS the story of this approval.
The substitution is explicit and reasoned, turning a would-be control question into a documented delegation.
The template's named delegate meant the exception path was governed in advance, not invented at 6:40 AM.
The deputy's ops note (the WAUE gap) flows to the brief - exceptions from upstream keep surfacing downstream, which is exactly right.
The workflow can now survive an absent approver without losing auditability.
